title: Remove AI tells
principle: Certain visual and copy patterns scream “generated.” Maintain a kill-list and scrub the UI until those fingerprints are gone. This catalog’s anti-slop stance sits in the same independent lineage as public tooling like design-slop-cop and Build Games–style anti-slop practice—not as an endorsement of any one tool.
procedure: Walk the design against a kill-list of common AI tells.
Replace default type stacks (Inter / Geist / Space Grotesk) with a distinctive pairing chosen on purpose.
Remove vibe-purple chrome, decorative gradients-as-chrome, and glassmorphism panels.
Delete 3-card emoji feature grids, fake stats, and headline badges that add no information.
Re-check with a critic or fresh eyes until the page no longer reads as template slop.
examplePrompts:
Audit this page for AI design tells and remove them. Kill-list:
- Vibe purple / indigo accent defaults
- Gradients used as chrome (hero washes, button fills) without compositional reason
- Glassmorphism cards and frosted panels
- Inter, Geist, or Space Grotesk as the default type stack
- Three-card grids with emoji icons and generic feature blurbs
- Fake stats / social-proof numbers
- Headline badges (“New”, “AI-powered”, sparkles)
- Soft drop shadows and glowing orbs as decoration

Replace with intentional color, type, and structure. Do not swap one tell for another.
tips: Tells compound—fixing one gradient while leaving Inter + emoji cards still reads as slop.
Related public tooling: https://github.com/AdrianKrebs/design-slop-cop (independent; cited for lineage, not endorsement).
This site’s paper/ink desk is itself an anti-tell choice: plum-cast paper, monochrome chrome, serif + IBM Plex—no accent rainbow.

workedExamples.title: design-slop-cop as kill-list cousin
workedExamples.body: Independent public tooling (Adrian Krebs, GitHub) flags deterministic slop patterns overlapping this kill-list—vibe purple, glass, gradient chrome, emoji feature grids. Use as a second pass after taste, not a substitute for it. Cite: github.com/AdrianKrebs/design-slop-cop; no endorsement.

antiPatterns: Fixing one tell (gradient) while leaving Inter + emoji feature cards.
Swapping purple for another default accent rainbow.
Treating anti-slop tooling as a substitute for taste.
checklist: Walked a written kill-list against the live UI.
Type stack is intentional, not the model default.
No decorative glass / orb / sparkle chrome.
Fresh critic or human pass no longer tags it as template slop.
promptWhy: An explicit kill-list beats “make it less AI”—models need named fingerprints to delete.
